desc: Enable panel backlight control, which a daily driver needs and which is currently absent. MEASURED: the full kernel has CONFIG_BACKLIGHT_CLASS_DEVICE=y but CONFIG_APPLE_DWI_BL is ABSENT from config-hid-type-fix, so there is no backlight device at all — brightness is stuck wherever iBoot left it. The driver exists in-tree (drivers/video/backlight/apple_dwi_bl.c appears in the MAINTAINERS Apple section). TASK: enable APPLE_DWI_BL in the kernel config, confirm the J614s DT actually describes the DWI backlight node (check t6040-j614s-dcuart.dts and the ADT for a dwi/backlight node — if absent, the DT work is the real task and the kernel symbol alone will do nothing), then verify /sys/class/backlight/*/brightness responds. Read/write of a backlight is not a PMU or charger write, so it is inside policy. Pair with 165 so dwm can bind brightness keys. KEYBOARD BACKLIGHT CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-08-03 (CJ visually verified the keys light up). Path: ADT /arm-io/pwm0/kbd-backlight decoded as a plain s5l fpwm (nits-to-pwm tables + default-hz 25000 = the 40000 ns j293 period), wired as fpwm0@429040000 + a pwm-leds node in the wifi DTS, PWM_APPLE/LEDS_PWM builtin. Live: /sys/class/leds/kbd_backlight, max_brightness 255, echo 255 > brightness lights the keys. brightnessctl and most DEs will find it. PANEL backlight remains separate and DCP-blocked (ticket 022).
author: claude
note: 2026-07-27 NOT the simple win I scoped. apple_dwi_bl.c binds 'apple,dwi-bl', but that binding is only used on iPhone/iPad-era SoCs (s5l8960x, s8001, t7000, t8010, t8015). On Apple Silicon MACBOOKS the panel backlight is generally tied to the internal display via the DCP, not DWI. The t6040 ADT DOES have a 'dwi' node (dwi,t8101 at cpu 0x5029b0000, irq 273), but whether it drives the J614s panel backlight vs the DCP path is UNVERIFIED. Authoring a dwi-bl DT node blind risks a non-functional or wrong backlight. NEEDS: confirm the J614s backlight path (check how Asahi wires MacBook backlight — likely dcp/dcpext + a backlight child, or apple,smc) before authoring. Not safely autonomous without that.
